Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and appreciate the clarity on the four core success criteria (accuracy on clinical Q&A, hallucination reduction, sub-200ms median latency target for 95% of requests, and predictable unit cost). Per our demo and the eval highlights, I pulled together a recommended model shortlist with rationale and next steps so we can kick off an apples-to-apples eval. See attachments and links below.

Shortlist (tradeoffs at a glance) — all are available in Redwood’s catalog and we can run the evals on Dedicated or Private per your preference:

1) Mistral-Instruct-7B-v1 (quantized) — best-in-class cost/latency for instruction-following tasks
   - Quality: strong for instruction tuning and short-form Q&A after light prompt tuning
   - Latency: sub-100ms median on 1xA10-like instance with Redwood batching
   - Cost: lowest per-token among shortlist; good candidate for high-throughput endpoints
   - When to pick: if you need high volume support and are willing to add a second-stage verifier for edge hallucinations

2) Llama 2 13B Chat (4-bit quant)
   - Quality: higher factual accuracy on long-context clinical prompts after prompt engineering
   - Latency: ~120-180ms median depending on sequence length and KV cache warmness
   - Cost: mid-range; good balance of quality vs cost
   - When to pick: primary candidate if accuracy is prioritized but cost still matters

3) Redwood-3.1-realtime-8B (internal name) — tuned + safety-checked variant
   - Quality: best out-of-the-box on clinical Q&A (fewer hallucinations in our internal evals)
   - Latency: ~110ms median, robust under bursty traffic with autoscaling policies
   - Cost: slightly above Mistral-7B but lower than 13B models; includes Redwood safety filters
   - When to pick: teams that want better safety/quality with predictable latency and minimal prompt engineering

Benchmarks & artifacts included:
- Attachment: 20260818_acme_benchmarks.pdf (summary of per-model ROUGE/EM-style scores, hallucination counts, latency percentiles on sample workload)
- Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (the prompt/eval set we used during the demo; please flag any PHI/PII we should redact)
- Eval notebook (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeEval

Suggested next steps:
- You: confirm the prompt set and any changes (redaction, extra examples) — if ok we’ll run a 1k-example eval across the shortlist
- Redwood: run the 1k eval (David will own), produce a per-model rubric (accuracy/hallucination/latency/cost), and schedule a follow-up to review results (30–45 minutes)
- Optional: two-week POC on Dedicated with production traffic replay if the eval looks good (we can scope cost separately)

Open questions from our side:
- Do you have any strict throughput/peak qps numbers we should simulate?
- Are there any redlines for data residency/compliance (HIPAA specifics) beyond what we discussed?

I’ll loop David in to handle the eval and Rishi for CS and pricing. Happy to adjust the shortlist based on your priorities.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A few quick follow-ups from our end: 

- Hallucination metrics: can you share the specific definition you used in the benchmark (e.g., factual error rate vs. unverifiable statements)? We need to map that to our clinical review process.
- Latency/SLO: our product team wants to hold to a 200ms p95 for typical single-turn queries — curious how the models behave at p95 under a simulated 50 qps load.
- Data/redaction: we will scrub direct PHI but may need to test with partially redacted examples. Can you confirm Redwood’s handling of partially redacted inputs for eval workloads?

Also, Tom asked about sample outputs — can you include 3–5 example responses from each model on the prompt set so our clinical reviewers can eyeball the differences?

If all that looks ok we’re happy to move forward with the 1k eval.

—Sofia
